name: IRONLIMB VertexCore Titanium Spinal Column
description:
The VertexCore replaces the lumbar and thoracic vertebrae with a segmented titanium-alloy column, surgically anchored to the pelvis and skull-base via shock-absorbing ceramic endplates. Each vertebral unit is independently load-rated to 800kg compression, with embedded piezoelectric sensors that detect spinal compression events and stiffen the column in milliseconds to prevent crush injury. Micro-hydraulic dampers between segments absorb axial shock from falls or blunt trauma, and a passive neural bypass reroutes signals around damaged cord sections if injury occurs.

VertexCore is the default prescription for laborers, freight handlers, and construction workers who suffer industrial crush injuries or degenerative disc disease from decades of Shelf-tier physical labor. It has no aesthetic appeal—the hardware is purely functional, and the surgery leaves a visible ridge along the back—but among Fenris dock crews and Tier 1-2 workers, a VertexCore scar is worn as a badge of survival. IRONLIMB markets it bluntly: "Your spine was broken. Now it isn't."
installation_requirements: Full spinal surgery under general anesthesia, 6-8 hour procedure, orthopedic-neuro surgical team, 3-month recovery
rejection_risk: Low — titanium alloy is highly biocompatible; ceramic endplates promote osseointegration
maintenance: Annual compression calibration; hydraulic damper fluid replacement every 3 years

side_effects: Reduced lateral spinal flexibility — twisting range limited to ~60% of baseline
Thermal sensitivity in cold environments as metal conducts ambient temperature
Audible faint clicking during heavy load shifts
Permanent visible dorsal ridge under skin
cultural_context: On the Shelf, a VertexCore is often the difference between continued employment and permanent disability. Ironlimb's financing plans are notorious—workers sign multi-year wage garnishment agreements to afford the surgery, creating a debt cycle that critics call 'spinal indentured servitude.' Labor organizers sometimes use the scar as a rallying symbol.
known_users: Industrial laborers and freight dock workers
Construction crews on high-rise Spire projects
story_hooks: A VertexCore unit has been recalled due to a batch defect causing hydraulic fluid leakage into the spinal canal — thousands of workers are quietly going numb, and IRONLIMB is suppressing the reports
A labor organizer with a VertexCore is using the embedded piezoelectric sensors as a hidden data recorder, storing evidence of workplace safety violations in the hardware itself
